# FIX-ORI-AI-002-1: Take the NativeWind driver's turn records baselines before each send flow

## What this does

Fixes the records-baseline ordering defect in the ORI-RN-005-owned NativeWind live-proof driver (`tests/sprint-05-orient-search/support/nativewind-live-example.ts`) that blocks ORI-AI-002's six-target matrix. Observed in ORI-AI-002's cycle-4 attempts c4e/c4g/c4h (3/3 reproductions on freshly rebooted devices; diagnostics in `tests/sprint-05-orient-search/evidence/ORI-AI-002/server-events.jsonl` phase-end legs and `.tmp/ORI-AI-002/cycle-4/red/`): with a caller-provided backend, the iOS leg's marker turn fails as `marker turn ended as no terminal record` while the marker's completed provider record — completed in ~1.7 s — is present in the same run's records.

Code facts at main `cbb782d2`: `runIosInputFlow`'s `awaitTurn` closure (lines 1573-1584) captures `const baseline = session.current.records().length` at await time, and its call sites drive `sendTurn('marker'|'seed'|'follow-up', …)` — the synchronous one-off maestro flow — BEFORE `awaitTurn(…)` (lines 1621-1624, 1634-1637, 1644-1647). Any provider record landing during the maestro send flow's window sits at or before the await-time baseline, so the `records.length > baseline` terminal predicate in `awaitTerminalRecord` (line 934) and `sampleAssistantTextGrowth` (line 965) never fires and the await burns its full 120 s into a false "no terminal record". The same await-time capture exists in `handleTerminal`'s Retry recovery (line 1609, baseline after the Retry tap) and in the Android flow's Retry recoveries (lines 1226, 1256). The correct ordering already exists twice in this file: the stop-turn drives take the baseline BEFORE `runOneOffMaestroFlow` (line 1677), and the Android `runTurn` takes it before the send tap (line 1199). The fix moves every conversational-turn baseline capture to before the flow that issues the request — the `records.length > baseline` guard already makes a pre-send baseline semantically correct for both predicates (it skips every record at or below the baseline, so the baseline detects exactly the send's record whenever it lands), and for the Retry paths the failed turn's error record sits below a pre-tap baseline so only the retry's new record crosses it.

## Why

ORI-AI-002's cycle-4 blocked report (commit `d1f5d99e`, item `ORI-AI-002:blocked:4:scope_impact:0`) proves everything else in the six-target matrix is green at that checkpoint; the single remaining blocker is this driver-internal ordering defect, and the driver is write-prohibited to ORI-AI-002. ORI-RN-005 owns the file and is completed; FIX-ORI-RN-004-2 and FIX-ORI-RN-004-3 (both completed) fixed the sibling Uniwind driver, and this is the NativeWind counterpart's turn. No pending task owns the file. Once the ordering is fixed, ORI-AI-002's committed runner re-runs its two exact verify commands with no further work in its own files.

## How to verify

```sh
pnpm exec tsx tests/sprint-05-orient-search/nativewind-baseline-ordering-proof.test.ts
pnpm exec tsx tests/sprint-05-orient-search/nativewind-baseline-ordering-proof.test.ts --matrix ios,android,web
pnpm exec tsx tests/sprint-05-orient-search/support/nativewind-live-example.ts --case ORI-RN-005-install-exact-source
pnpm typecheck
pnpm exec biome ci tests/sprint-05-orient-search/support/nativewind-live-example.ts tests/sprint-05-orient-search/nativewind-baseline-ordering-proof.test.ts
```

The first command is the task-owned harness: it invokes the real driver exactly as ORI-AI-002's runner does (caller-created owned-backend handle, `platforms: ['ios']`, fresh run identity, watchdog) and proves the marker-turn record-lands-before-baseline failure pre-fix and its absence post-fix. The second is the regression gate: the harness's `--matrix ios,android,web` mode drives the driver's canonical three-platform matrix as a child under the harness watchdog. The third is this driver's own fast compiler/install case (the NativeWind analog of the sibling FIX tasks' ORI-RN-004 AC-5 gate; the Uniwind compiler case does not apply because this task never touches the Uniwind driver). The rest are static gates.

## Scope

Own the baseline-ordering fix in the NativeWind driver and the task-owned harness, plus bounded evidence. ORI-AI-002's runner, the Uniwind driver, the shared support files, and every in-flight file stay untouched; the fixed driver is consumed by ORI-AI-002's re-dispatch through the frozen `runNativewindLiveExampleProof` / `options.backend` interface.

### OUTCOME

The NativeWind driver's conversational-turn terminal awaits detect their turn's provider record regardless of when it lands: every marker/seed/follow-up await — and its Retry recovery — captures its records baseline BEFORE the flow that issues the request, mirroring the file's own stop-turn drives, so a record completing during the maestro send window terminates its await immediately instead of burning 120 s into a false "no terminal record"; ORI-AI-002's runner consumes the fixed driver unchanged through the frozen `runNativewindLiveExampleProof` / `options.backend` seam.

### CRITICAL CONSTRAINTS — Never

- Never weaken the terminal predicates: the `records.length > baseline` guard and the terminal-outcome sets stay as-is. The fix moves WHERE the baseline is captured, never WHAT the predicate accepts — dropping or widening the guard to make the await fire is an oracle weakening, not a fix.
- Never change the consumed interface: `runNativewindLiveExampleProof`'s exported signature and `ProofOptions` (including `options.backend: OwnedBackendHandle`, `runId`, `outputDir`, `manifestPath`, `sourceSha`), the `--platforms` / `--case` / `--run-id` / `--out` / `--manifest` CLI behavior, the `manifest.json` / `provider-correlation.json` / `teardown.json` schemas, and the BackendSession semantics stay behavior-identical. - Never mock the device, maestro, backend, or provider for the live lane; the RED reproduction is the real driver on the reserved simulator with a real caller-created owned-backend handle over the real provider.
- Never touch the stop-turn drive baselines (already correct), the endpoint-loss phases, the web leg, or the growth-sampling architecture.

# Sprint 05: orient-search

**Status:** in_progress  
**Sequence:** 5  
**Timeline:** Phase 2

## Overview

Give a first-time integrator a complete orientation path: Introduction, one engine decision, registry-specific installation and CLI guidance, Theming and Dark mode, one seed-data Quickstart, and a handoff to a real AI SDK v7 example. Connect that content to persistent engine tabs, live theme values, built-site search, registry destinations, and useful missing-page recovery.

Absorb the smallest real prerequisites that make those paths executable: the published PromptInput import graph, both clean Expo consumers, a substantive ownership explanation, actual 404 recovery, the real example API and native composition, canonical registry hosting, and source-bound build and publication checks. This does not add another tutorial or a demonstrated use case. Sprint 06 may deepen the ownership tables; Sprint 11 may deepen resilience and accessibility; later delivery work may harden deployment and rollback.

The plan contains **36 tasks / 131 points**, compared with the roadmap sketch of approximately 12 items / 34–55 points: **76 points above its upper bound**. It retains 13 locked flows, 13 numbered gate steps, and four post-integration journey proofs. Estimates describe the approved prerequisite absorption rather than forcing the work into the sketch.

All implementation, functional RED, product verification, hosted acceptance, and deployment proof are future work. This document records a plan, not a passing gate or release.

## Human Testing Gate

**Gate:** A stranger opening /docs/introduction over the built site's local preview can read in one pass that the library provides universal AI chat and agent UI components for React Native, that it is distributed as a copy-paste registry, and that it is not an npm package.

**Entrypoint:** docs site local preview — built dist served by astro preview (http://localhost:4321) or the pnpm e2e:docs webServer; route /docs/introduction

**Before:** The source snapshot at the planned source SHA already contains Theming and shared layout, header, table, and tab controls. Introduction, Installation, CLI, Dark mode, Quickstart, the ownership-boundary route, and a custom 404 route are absent in that inspected snapshot. Existing Theming content still needs engine-correct claims and the real paired TokenTable. These are planning observations from the source, not current browser results. Each owner must observe the actual functional failure before implementation; the stale roadmap claim that all of these controls are absent is not a RED oracle.

**Success state:** A visitor reads useful, source-backed bodies instead of empty shells, chooses the correct engine once, follows literal registry commands, reads the same information without JavaScript, sees live theme changes without a flash, and reaches real content through keyboard search or missing-page recovery. The single Quickstart reaches a visible seed-data screen and then a separately verified real-provider example. Acceptance also requires the discriminating build checks and fresh native, provider, public-registry, and hosted evidence specified below.

**Demonstrates:** UC-DOCS-01, UC-DOCS-02, UC-SHELL-02, UC-SHELL-01 (TokenTable half), UC-SHELL-03 (prose-persistence half)

**Fixed carryover:** UC-GEND-07 AC-2; TR-12 (full); CAP-DOCS-01 snippet/link build integration. Boundary, recovery, API, and publication work support this projection; they do not expand the demonstrated-use-case list.

# FIX-ORI-AI-002-1: Take the NativeWind driver's turn records baselines before each send flow

## What this does

Fixes the records-baseline ordering defect in the ORI-RN-005-owned NativeWind live-proof driver (`tests/sprint-05-orient-search/support/nativewind-live-example.ts`) that blocks ORI-AI-002's six-target matrix. Observed in ORI-AI-002's cycle-4 attempts c4e/c4g/c4h (3/3 reproductions on freshly rebooted devices; diagnostics in `tests/sprint-05-orient-search/evidence/ORI-AI-002/server-events.jsonl` phase-end legs and `.tmp/ORI-AI-002/cycle-4/red/`): with a caller-provided backend, the iOS leg's marker turn fails as `marker turn ended as no terminal record` while the marker's completed provider record — completed in ~1.7 s — is present in the same run's records.

Code facts at main `cbb782d2`: `runIosInputFlow`'s `awaitTurn` closure (lines 1573-1584) captures `const baseline = session.current.records().length` at await time, and its call sites drive `sendTurn('marker'|'seed'|'follow-up', …)` — the synchronous one-off maestro flow — BEFORE `awaitTurn(…)` (lines 1621-1624, 1634-1637, 1644-1647). Any provider record landing during the maestro send flow's window sits at or before the await-time baseline, so the `records.length > baseline` terminal predicate in `awaitTerminalRecord` (line 934) and `sampleAssistantTextGrowth` (line 965) never fires and the await burns its full 120 s into a false "no terminal record". The same await-time capture exists in `handleTerminal`'s Retry recovery (line 1609, baseline after the Retry tap) and in the Android flow's Retry recoveries (lines 1226, 1256). The correct ordering already exists twice in this file: the stop-turn drives take the baseline BEFORE `runOneOffMaestroFlow` (line 1677), and the Android `runTurn` takes it before the send tap (line 1199). The fix moves every conversational-turn baseline capture to before the flow that issues the request — the `records.length > baseline` guard already makes a pre-send baseline semantically correct for both predicates (it skips every record at or below the baseline, so the baseline detects exactly the send's record whenever it lands), and for the Retry paths the failed turn's error record sits below a pre-tap baseline so only the retry's new record crosses it.

## Why

ORI-AI-002's cycle-4 blocked report (commit `d1f5d99e`, item `ORI-AI-002:blocked:4:scope_impact:0`) proves everything else in the six-target matrix is green at that checkpoint; the single remaining blocker is this driver-internal ordering defect, and the driver is write-prohibited to ORI-AI-002. ORI-RN-005 owns the file and is completed; FIX-ORI-RN-004-2 and FIX-ORI-RN-004-3 (both completed) fixed the sibling Uniwind driver, and this is the NativeWind counterpart's turn. No pending task owns the file. Once the ordering is fixed, ORI-AI-002's committed runner re-runs its two exact verify commands with no further work in its own files.

## How to verify

```sh
pnpm exec tsx tests/sprint-05-orient-search/nativewind-baseline-ordering-proof.test.ts
pnpm exec tsx tests/sprint-05-orient-search/nativewind-baseline-ordering-proof.test.ts --matrix ios,android,web
pnpm exec tsx tests/sprint-05-orient-search/support/nativewind-live-example.ts --case ORI-RN-005-install-exact-source
pnpm typecheck
pnpm exec biome ci tests/sprint-05-orient-search/support/nativewind-live-example.ts tests/sprint-05-orient-search/nativewind-baseline-ordering-proof.test.ts
```

The first command is the task-owned harness: it invokes the real driver exactly as ORI-AI-002's runner does (caller-created owned-backend handle, `platforms: ['ios']`, fresh run identity, watchdog) and proves the marker-turn record-lands-before-baseline failure pre-fix and its absence post-fix. # Sprint 05: orient-search

**Status:** in_progress  
**Sequence:** 5  
**Timeline:** Phase 2

## Overview

Give a first-time integrator a complete orientation path: Introduction, one engine decision, registry-specific installation and CLI guidance, Theming and Dark mode, one seed-data Quickstart, and a handoff to a real AI SDK v7 example. Connect that content to persistent engine tabs, live theme values, built-site search, registry destinations, and useful missing-page recovery.

Absorb the smallest real prerequisites that make those paths executable: the published PromptInput import graph, both clean Expo consumers, a substantive ownership explanation, actual 404 recovery, the real example API and native composition, canonical registry hosting, and source-bound build and publication checks. This does not add another tutorial or a demonstrated use case. Sprint 06 may deepen the ownership tables; Sprint 11 may deepen resilience and accessibility; later delivery work may harden deployment and rollback.

The plan contains **36 tasks / 131 points**, compared with the roadmap sketch of approximately 12 items / 34–55 points: **76 points above its upper bound**. It retains 13 locked flows, 13 numbered gate steps, and four post-integration journey proofs. Estimates describe the approved prerequisite absorption rather than forcing the work into the sketch.

All implementation, functional RED, product verification, hosted acceptance, and deployment proof are future work. This document records a plan, not a passing gate or release.

## Human Testing Gate

**Gate:** A stranger opening /docs/introduction over the built site's local preview can read in one pass that the library provides universal AI chat and agent UI components for React Native, that it is distributed as a copy-paste registry, and that it is not an npm package.

**Entrypoint:** docs site local preview — built dist served by astro preview (http://localhost:4321) or the pnpm e2e:docs webServer; route /docs/introduction

**Before:** The source snapshot at the planned source SHA already contains Theming and shared layout, header, table, and tab controls. Introduction, Installation, CLI, Dark mode, Quickstart, the ownership-boundary route, and a custom 404 route are absent in that inspected snapshot. Existing Theming content still needs engine-correct claims and the real paired TokenTable. These are planning observations from the source, not current browser results. Each owner must observe the actual functional failure before implementation; the stale roadmap claim that all of these controls are absent is not a RED oracle.

**Success state:** A visitor reads useful, source-backed bodies instead of empty shells, chooses the correct engine once, follows literal registry commands, reads the same information without JavaScript, sees live theme changes without a flash, and reaches real content through keyboard search or missing-page recovery. The single Quickstart reaches a visible seed-data screen and then a separately verified real-provider example. Acceptance also requires the discriminating build checks and fresh native, provider, public-registry, and hosted evidence specified below.

**Demonstrates:** UC-DOCS-01, UC-DOCS-02, UC-SHELL-02, UC-SHELL-01 (TokenTable half), UC-SHELL-03 (prose-persistence half)

**Fixed carryover:** UC-GEND-07 AC-2; TR-12 (full); CAP-DOCS-01 snippet/link build integration. Boundary, recovery, API, and publication work support this projection; they do not expand the demonstrated-use-case list.

# FIX-ORI-CI-001-1: Author the Quickstart tutorial designation and land its schema field

## What this does

Lands the one-line tutorial designation that no task in the prerequisite chain ever owned: `tutorial: true` in the `apps/docs/src/content/docs/quickstart.mdx` frontmatter, plus the schema field that carries it — `tutorial: z.boolean().optional()` in the `apps/docs/src/content.config.ts` docs collection schema. Two lines total, verified by the real docs build.

ORI-CI-001's cycle-1 blocked report (commit `41a496019097428987e628863763716776026179`, item `ORI-CI-001:blocked:1:scope_impact:0`) records the gap: boundary contract 5 of ORI-CI-001's charter states "ORI-CONT-003 authors tutorial: true against the declared schema contract", but ORI-CONT-003's own task file contains no such requirement (its deviations record only `order: 2.5`) and ORI-AST-001 explicitly scoped tutorial cardinality enforcement out — the prerequisite chain has a hole, and authored content is write-prohibited to the in-flight ORI-CI-001. Orchestrator-verified trunk facts: the quickstart.mdx frontmatter carries only title/description/section/order(2.5), and the schema declares title/description/section/order/draft with no tutorial field, so ORI-CI-001's landed fail-closed gate would count 0 published tutorials against the required 1 and could never be wired without breaking every docs build.

The schema line is not new code: ORI-CI-001's cycle-1 checkpoint (41a49601) already proved `tutorial: z.boolean().optional()` behavior-neutral on the real build (`pnpm --filter @rnr-ai-elements/docs build` exit 0 at 67 pages). This task lands that exact line on trunk; when ORI-CI-001's branch later merges trunk, the identical line reconciles cleanly.

## Why

ORI-CONT-003 (completed — approved 22780223, merged 3635ba62) landed the Quickstart manuscript but was never contractually tasked with the designation; ORI-AST-001 scoped cardinality enforcement out; ORI-CI-001 owns the enforcement machinery but is content-write-prohibited. Every path to wiring the single-tutorial gate runs through this missing line, and the sprint's dark proof row ORI-CI-001 ("the actual build rejects duplicate, missing, and noncanonical published tutorials, then accepts the restored single tutorial") is unreachable while the count observes 0. No pending task owns either file for this purpose. This is the smallest content-authorized change that closes the gap: two lines, no gate wiring, no behavior change to any consumer that does not yet read the field.

## How to verify

```sh
pnpm --filter @rnr-ai-elements/docs build
pnpm typecheck
pnpm exec biome ci apps/docs/src/content.config.ts
```

The first command is the real public docs build (registry + gallery + astro build). RED captures the pre-change trunk state with that same command — exit 0 at the observed page count with 0 designation occurrences in both files. GREEN reruns the identical command after the two lines land. The carrier proof is a scratch-copy negative pair under an owned `os.tmpdir()` root: removing only the frontmatter line leaves the build green with 0 carriers (the line is the sole carrier, and the build alone does not enforce the designation — ORI-CI-001's gate owns that), while changing the value to the non-boolean `tutorial: 'yes'` fails the real build with a collection-validation diagnostic naming the docs collection, the quickstart source, and the `tutorial` field path. The rest are static gates.

## Scope

Own exactly two repository lines plus bounded evidence. The single-tutorial gate stays unwired: no `[...id].astro` import, no `scripts/docs-data/single-tutorial.ts` on trunk, no subprocess drill, no evidence files under `tests/sprint-05-orient-search/evidence/ORI-CI-001/` — all of that remains ORI-CI-001's cycle-2 work, which this task unblocks.

# Sprint 05: orient-search

**Status:** in_progress  
**Sequence:** 5  
**Timeline:** Phase 2

## Overview

Give a first-time integrator a complete orientation path: Introduction, one engine decision, registry-specific installation and CLI guidance, Theming and Dark mode, one seed-data Quickstart, and a handoff to a real AI SDK v7 example. Connect that content to persistent engine tabs, live theme values, built-site search, registry destinations, and useful missing-page recovery.

Absorb the smallest real prerequisites that make those paths executable: the published PromptInput import graph, both clean Expo consumers, a substantive ownership explanation, actual 404 recovery, the real example API and native composition, canonical registry hosting, and source-bound build and publication checks. This does not add another tutorial or a demonstrated use case. Sprint 06 may deepen the ownership tables; Sprint 11 may deepen resilience and accessibility; later delivery work may harden deployment and rollback.

The plan contains **36 tasks / 131 points**, compared with the roadmap sketch of approximately 12 items / 34–55 points: **76 points above its upper bound**. It retains 13 locked flows, 13 numbered gate steps, and four post-integration journey proofs. Estimates describe the approved prerequisite absorption rather than forcing the work into the sketch.

All implementation, functional RED, product verification, hosted acceptance, and deployment proof are future work. This document records a plan, not a passing gate or release.

## Human Testing Gate

**Gate:** A stranger opening /docs/introduction over the built site's local preview can read in one pass that the library provides universal AI chat and agent UI components for React Native, that it is distributed as a copy-paste registry, and that it is not an npm package.

**Entrypoint:** docs site local preview — built dist served by astro preview (http://localhost:4321) or the pnpm e2e:docs webServer; route /docs/introduction

**Before:** The source snapshot at the planned source SHA already contains Theming and shared layout, header, table, and tab controls. Introduction, Installation, CLI, Dark mode, Quickstart, the ownership-boundary route, and a custom 404 route are absent in that inspected snapshot. Existing Theming content still needs engine-correct claims and the real paired TokenTable. These are planning observations from the source, not current browser results. Each owner must observe the actual functional failure before implementation; the stale roadmap claim that all of these controls are absent is not a RED oracle.

**Success state:** A visitor reads useful, source-backed bodies instead of empty shells, chooses the correct engine once, follows literal registry commands, reads the same information without JavaScript, sees live theme changes without a flash, and reaches real content through keyboard search or missing-page recovery. The single Quickstart reaches a visible seed-data screen and then a separately verified real-provider example. Acceptance also requires the discriminating build checks and fresh native, provider, public-registry, and hosted evidence specified below.

**Demonstrates:** UC-DOCS-01, UC-DOCS-02, UC-SHELL-02, UC-SHELL-01 (TokenTable half), UC-SHELL-03 (prose-persistence half)

**Fixed carryover:** UC-GEND-07 AC-2; TR-12 (full); CAP-DOCS-01 snippet/link build integration. Boundary, recovery, API, and publication work support this projection; they do not expand the demonstrated-use-case list.

# FIX-ORI-CI-001-1: Author the Quickstart tutorial designation and land its schema field

## What this does

Lands the one-line tutorial designation that no task in the prerequisite chain ever owned: `tutorial: true` in the `apps/docs/src/content/docs/quickstart.mdx` frontmatter, plus the schema field that carries it — `tutorial: z.boolean().optional()` in the `apps/docs/src/content.config.ts` docs collection schema. Two lines total, verified by the real docs build.

ORI-CI-001's cycle-1 blocked report (commit `41a496019097428987e628863763716776026179`, item `ORI-CI-001:blocked:1:scope_impact:0`) records the gap: boundary contract 5 of ORI-CI-001's charter states "ORI-CONT-003 authors tutorial: true against the declared schema contract", but ORI-CONT-003's own task file contains no such requirement (its deviations record only `order: 2.5`) and ORI-AST-001 explicitly scoped tutorial cardinality enforcement out — the prerequisite chain has a hole, and authored content is write-prohibited to the in-flight ORI-CI-001. Orchestrator-verified trunk facts: the quickstart.mdx frontmatter carries only title/description/section/order(2.5), and the schema declares title/description/section/order/draft with no tutorial field, so ORI-CI-001's landed fail-closed gate would count 0 published tutorials against the required 1 and could never be wired without breaking every docs build.

The schema line is not new code: ORI-CI-001's cycle-1 checkpoint (41a49601) already proved `tutorial: z.boolean().optional()` behavior-neutral on the real build (`pnpm --filter @rnr-ai-elements/docs build` exit 0 at 67 pages). This task lands that exact line on trunk; when ORI-CI-001's branch later merges trunk, the identical line reconciles cleanly.

## Why

ORI-CONT-003 (completed — approved 22780223, merged 3635ba62) landed the Quickstart manuscript but was never contractually tasked with the designation; ORI-AST-001 scoped cardinality enforcement out; ORI-CI-001 owns the enforcement machinery but is content-write-prohibited. Every path to wiring the single-tutorial gate runs through this missing line, and the sprint's dark proof row ORI-CI-001 ("the actual build rejects duplicate, missing, and noncanonical published tutorials, then accepts the restored single tutorial") is unreachable while the count observes 0. No pending task owns either file for this purpose. This is the smallest content-authorized change that closes the gap: two lines, no gate wiring, no behavior change to any consumer that does not yet read the field.

## How to verify

```sh
pnpm --filter @rnr-ai-elements/docs build
pnpm typecheck
pnpm exec biome ci apps/docs/src/content.config.ts
```

The first command is the real public docs build (registry + gallery + astro build). RED captures the pre-change trunk state with that same command — exit 0 at the observed page count with 0 designation occurrences in both files. GREEN reruns the identical command after the two lines land. The carrier proof is a scratch-copy negative pair under an owned `os.tmpdir()` root: removing only the frontmatter line leaves the build green with 0 carriers (the line is the sole carrier, and the build alone does not enforce the designation — ORI-CI-001's gate owns that), while changing the value to the non-boolean `tutorial: 'yes'` fails the real build with a collection-validation diagnostic naming the docs collection, the quickstart source, and the `tutorial` field path. The rest are static gates.

## Scope

Own exactly two repository lines plus bounded evidence. The single-tutorial gate stays unwired: no `[...id].astro` import, no `scripts/docs-data/single-tutorial.ts` on trunk, no subprocess drill, no evidence files under `tests/sprint-05-orient-search/evidence/ORI-CI-001/` — all of that remains ORI-CI-001's cycle-2 work, which this task unblocks.

# Sprint 05: orient-search

**Status:** in_progress  
**Sequence:** 5  
**Timeline:** Phase 2

## Overview

Give a first-time integrator a complete orientation path: Introduction, one engine decision, registry-specific installation and CLI guidance, Theming and Dark mode, one seed-data Quickstart, and a handoff to a real AI SDK v7 example. Connect that content to persistent engine tabs, live theme values, built-site search, registry destinations, and useful missing-page recovery.

Absorb the smallest real prerequisites that make those paths executable: the published PromptInput import graph, both clean Expo consumers, a substantive ownership explanation, actual 404 recovery, the real example API and native composition, canonical registry hosting, and source-bound build and publication checks. This does not add another tutorial or a demonstrated use case. Sprint 06 may deepen the ownership tables; Sprint 11 may deepen resilience and accessibility; later delivery work may harden deployment and rollback.

The plan contains **36 tasks / 131 points**, compared with the roadmap sketch of approximately 12 items / 34–55 points: **76 points above its upper bound**. It retains 13 locked flows, 13 numbered gate steps, and four post-integration journey proofs. Estimates describe the approved prerequisite absorption rather than forcing the work into the sketch.

All implementation, functional RED, product verification, hosted acceptance, and deployment proof are future work. This document records a plan, not a passing gate or release.

## Human Testing Gate

**Gate:** A stranger opening /docs/introduction over the built site's local preview can read in one pass that the library provides universal AI chat and agent UI components for React Native, that it is distributed as a copy-paste registry, and that it is not an npm package.

**Entrypoint:** docs site local preview — built dist served by astro preview (http://localhost:4321) or the pnpm e2e:docs webServer; route /docs/introduction

**Before:** The source snapshot at the planned source SHA already contains Theming and shared layout, header, table, and tab controls. Introduction, Installation, CLI, Dark mode, Quickstart, the ownership-boundary route, and a custom 404 route are absent in that inspected snapshot. Existing Theming content still needs engine-correct claims and the real paired TokenTable. These are planning observations from the source, not current browser results. Each owner must observe the actual functional failure before implementation; the stale roadmap claim that all of these controls are absent is not a RED oracle.

**Success state:** A visitor reads useful, source-backed bodies instead of empty shells, chooses the correct engine once, follows literal registry commands, reads the same information without JavaScript, sees live theme changes without a flash, and reaches real content through keyboard search or missing-page recovery. The single Quickstart reaches a visible seed-data screen and then a separately verified real-provider example. Acceptance also requires the discriminating build checks and fresh native, provider, public-registry, and hosted evidence specified below.

**Demonstrates:** UC-DOCS-01, UC-DOCS-02, UC-SHELL-02, UC-SHELL-01 (TokenTable half), UC-SHELL-03 (prose-persistence half)

**Fixed carryover:** UC-GEND-07 AC-2; TR-12 (full); CAP-DOCS-01 snippet/link build integration. Boundary, recovery, API, and publication work support this projection; they do not expand the demonstrated-use-case list.

# FIX-ORI-CI-001-1: Author the Quickstart tutorial designation and land its schema field

## What this does

Lands the one-line tutorial designation that no task in the prerequisite chain ever owned: `tutorial: true` in the `apps/docs/src/content/docs/quickstart.mdx` frontmatter, plus the schema field that carries it — `tutorial: z.boolean().optional()` in the `apps/docs/src/content.config.ts` docs collection schema. Two product lines total, verified through a minimal task-owned proof harness (`tests/sprint-05-orient-search/tutorial-designation-proof.test.ts`) that drives the real docs build.

ORI-CI-001's cycle-1 blocked report (commit `41a496019097428987e628863763716776026179`, item `ORI-CI-001:blocked:1:scope_impact:0`) records the gap: boundary contract 5 of ORI-CI-001's charter states "ORI-CONT-003 authors tutorial: true against the declared schema contract", but ORI-CONT-003's own task file contains no such requirement (its deviations record only `order: 2.5`) and ORI-AST-001 explicitly scoped tutorial cardinality enforcement out — the prerequisite chain has a hole, and authored content is write-prohibited to the in-flight ORI-CI-001. Orchestrator-verified trunk facts: the quickstart.mdx frontmatter carries only title/description/section/order(2.5), and the schema declares title/description/section/order/draft with no tutorial field, so ORI-CI-001's landed fail-closed gate would count 0 published tutorials against the required 1 and could never be wired without breaking every docs build.

The schema line is not new code: ORI-CI-001's cycle-1 checkpoint (41a49601) already proved `tutorial: z.boolean().optional()` behavior-neutral on the real build (`pnpm --filter @rnr-ai-elements/docs build` exit 0 at 67 pages). This task lands that exact line on trunk; when ORI-CI-001's branch later merges trunk, the identical line reconciles cleanly.

## Why

ORI-CONT-003 (completed — approved 22780223, merged 3635ba62) landed the Quickstart manuscript but was never contractually tasked with the designation; ORI-AST-001 scoped cardinality enforcement out; ORI-CI-001 owns the enforcement machinery but is content-write-prohibited. Every path to wiring the single-tutorial gate runs through this missing line, and the sprint's dark proof row ORI-CI-001 ("the actual build rejects duplicate, missing, and noncanonical published tutorials, then accepts the restored single tutorial") is unreachable while the count observes 0. No pending task owns either file for this purpose. This is the smallest content-authorized change that closes the gap: two lines, no gate wiring, no behavior change to any consumer that does not yet read the field.

## How to verify

```sh
pnpm exec tsx tests/sprint-05-orient-search/tutorial-designation-proof.test.ts
pnpm typecheck
pnpm exec biome ci apps/docs/src/content.config.ts
```

The first command is the exact selector: a minimal task-owned proof harness that orchestrates the real commands and captures the evidence — (a) it runs the real `pnpm --filter @rnr-ai-elements/docs build` (registry + gallery + astro build) as a child and asserts exit 0 at the observed page-count literal (67 at planning time), (b) it counts `tutorial: true` occurrences in the source frontmatter — exactly 1 post-change, 0 pre-change as the RED, (c) it asserts `tutorial` occurs >= 1 time in the build-regenerated `apps/docs/.astro/content.d.ts` (0 pre-change), and (d) it executes the scratch-copy negative pair under an owned `os.tmpdir()` root: removing only the frontmatter line leaves the build green with 0 carriers (the line is the sole carrier, and the build alone does not enforce the designation — ORI-CI-001's gate owns that), while changing the value to the non-boolean `tutorial: 'yes'` fails the real build with a collection-validation diagnostic naming the docs collection, the quickstart source, and the `tutorial` field path. The harness stays small — it orchestrates the real commands and does not become a second gate. `pnpm typecheck` and the scoped Biome command are preserved static gates.

## Scope

Own exactly two repository lines, the task-owned proof harness, plus bounded evidence. The single-tutorial gate stays unwired: no `[...id].astro` import, no `scripts/docs-data/single-tutorial.ts` on trunk, no subprocess drill, no evidence files under `tests/sprint-05-orient-search/evidence/ORI-CI-001/` — all of that remains ORI-CI-001's cycle-2 work, which this task unblocks.

# Sprint 05: orient-search

**Status:** in_progress  
**Sequence:** 5  
**Timeline:** Phase 2

## Overview

Give a first-time integrator a complete orientation path: Introduction, one engine decision, registry-specific installation and CLI guidance, Theming and Dark mode, one seed-data Quickstart, and a handoff to a real AI SDK v7 example. Connect that content to persistent engine tabs, live theme values, built-site search, registry destinations, and useful missing-page recovery.

Absorb the smallest real prerequisites that make those paths executable: the published PromptInput import graph, both clean Expo consumers, a substantive ownership explanation, actual 404 recovery, the real example API and native composition, canonical registry hosting, and source-bound build and publication checks. This does not add another tutorial or a demonstrated use case. Sprint 06 may deepen the ownership tables; Sprint 11 may deepen resilience and accessibility; later delivery work may harden deployment and rollback.

The plan contains **36 tasks / 131 points**, compared with the roadmap sketch of approximately 12 items / 34–55 points: **76 points above its upper bound**. It retains 13 locked flows, 13 numbered gate steps, and four post-integration journey proofs. Estimates describe the approved prerequisite absorption rather than forcing the work into the sketch.

All implementation, functional RED, product verification, hosted acceptance, and deployment proof are future work. This document records a plan, not a passing gate or release.

## Human Testing Gate

**Gate:** A stranger opening /docs/introduction over the built site's local preview can read in one pass that the library provides universal AI chat and agent UI components for React Native, that it is distributed as a copy-paste registry, and that it is not an npm package.

**Entrypoint:** docs site local preview — built dist served by astro preview (http://localhost:4321) or the pnpm e2e:docs webServer; route /docs/introduction

**Before:** The source snapshot at the planned source SHA already contains Theming and shared layout, header, table, and tab controls. Introduction, Installation, CLI, Dark mode, Quickstart, the ownership-boundary route, and a custom 404 route are absent in that inspected snapshot. Existing Theming content still needs engine-correct claims and the real paired TokenTable. These are planning observations from the source, not current browser results. Each owner must observe the actual functional failure before implementation; the stale roadmap claim that all of these controls are absent is not a RED oracle.

**Success state:** A visitor reads useful, source-backed bodies instead of empty shells, chooses the correct engine once, follows literal registry commands, reads the same information without JavaScript, sees live theme changes without a flash, and reaches real content through keyboard search or missing-page recovery. The single Quickstart reaches a visible seed-data screen and then a separately verified real-provider example. Acceptance also requires the discriminating build checks and fresh native, provider, public-registry, and hosted evidence specified below.

**Demonstrates:** UC-DOCS-01, UC-DOCS-02, UC-SHELL-02, UC-SHELL-01 (TokenTable half), UC-SHELL-03 (prose-persistence half)

# FIX-ORI-AST-004-1: Publish the docs-owned streamdown dependency-explainer destination

## What this does

Lands the one destination the locked search contract names but no task ever owned: a docs-owned, hand-authored dependency explainer at `apps/docs/src/pages/components/streamdown.astro`, served at `/components/streamdown`. ORI-AST-004's pinned search-dialog contract (AC-1..4) and the locked gate flows (`human-flows.json:730,742` — "five existing item destinations" including `/components/streamdown`) treat that route as a real destination: Enter navigation must land at HTTP 200 with a rendered title, and the real Pagefind index must surface it for the query `streamdown`. The registry's 56 items never included streamdown — it is the third-party markdown-rendering dependency the conversation family consumes through the renderMarkdown seam, not a shippable registry item — so the generated `[item].astro` fan-out can never emit the route. This task authors the page directly (a static route wins over the `[item]` dynamic route without touching it), verified through a task-owned proof harness (`tests/sprint-05-orient-search/streamdown-destination-proof.test.ts`) that drives the real build, the pinned real Pagefind run, and the real built preview.

The page is honestly framed: it explains what Streamdown is (the npm package `react-native-streamdown`), why the conversation family depends on it (`MessageResponse` in Message and `ReasoningContent` in Reasoning take a `renderMarkdown` prop; omit it and each renders plain Text, and markdown repair runs before either), how a consumer installs it (the four peers and permissions rendered from the committed `apps/docs/src/data/dev-client-matrix.json` streamdown entry, plus the dev-client verdict), and its registry relationship through the pinned sentence `Streamdown is not a registry item.` — no registry CLI command, no `rnraielements.com/r/{engine}/streamdown.json` target, no InstallCommand, no version chip, no family pager.

## Why

ORI-AST-004 (in flight, blocked cycle 1, checkpoint `b2560ce3`) proved the entire search dialog against the real index — 7 passed / 8 failed, and all 8 failures are the single pinned `/components/streamdown` destination leg: the route is a verified 404 and searching streamdown returns only the two docs pages that mention it. The wave-4 ruling made the resolution human-owned; the human decided (recorded in-session 2026-09-25) to create the docs-owned destination page rather than amend three tasks' ACs plus locked gate steps. Every path to ORI-AST-004's GREEN runs through this page existing at that route in the built dist and the real index. ORI-AST-008 (completed — commit `f5586742`) owns the reference-destination surface whose conventions this page follows; ORI-CONT-005 (completed) authored the boundary prose the page restates and links to. The search dialog, the indexer script, and the page model are write-prohibited to this task — they land with ORI-AST-004's branch, whose eight failing legs flip green once this page reaches trunk.

## How to verify

```sh
pnpm exec tsx tests/sprint-05-orient-search/streamdown-destination-proof.test.ts
pnpm typecheck
pnpm exec biome ci apps/docs/src/pages/components/streamdown.astro tests/sprint-05-orient-search/streamdown-destination-proof.test.ts
```

The first command is the exact selector: the task-owned proof harness — (a) RED phase: on the pre-change candidate it runs the real `pnpm --filter @rnr-ai-elements/docs build`, the pinned real Pagefind run (`pnpm dlx pagefind@1.5.2 --site apps/docs/dist`, the identical invocation ORI-AST-004's indexer uses), and the real built preview over the dist, recording the route's 404, the build page count, and the index page_count; (b) GREEN phase: identical commands with the page landed — build exit 0 at RED page count + 1, HTTP 200 at `/components/streamdown` with the rendered h1 carrying Streamdown and the pinned honest sentence, index page_count exactly RED + 1 (63 → 64 as it lands), and zero registry-command occurrences in the served HTML. The harness stays small — it orchestrates the real commands and does not become a second search gate. `pnpm typecheck` and the scoped Biome command are preserved static gates.

## Scope

Own exactly the new destination page, the task-owned proof harness, plus bounded evidence. The search dialog, `scripts/docs-data/search-index.ts`, `apps/docs/src/lib/search-page-model.ts`, the `[item].astro` template, every existing page, and `human-flows.json` stay byte-unchanged — the locked gate flows now point at a route that will exist; their bytes stay locked.

Content, all source-backed: what Streamdown is (the third-party markdown renderer for streaming markdown in React Native, published as the npm package `react-native-streamdown`); why the conversation family depends on it (`MessageResponse` in Message and `ReasoningContent` in Reasoning accept a `renderMarkdown` prop — omit it and each renders plain Text; markdown repair runs before either, per the landed boundary prose); how a consumer installs it (the four peers, the iOS/Android permissions, and the dev-client verdict rendered from the committed `dev-client-matrix.json` entry `id: "streamdown"` — `react-native-streamdown@0.3.0`, `react-native-enriched-markdown@>=1.0.0`, `react-native-worklets@>=0.10.0`, `remend@1.3.0`); and the honest registry relationship through the pinned sentence `Streamdown is not a registry item.` with the explanation that no `rnraielements.com/r/{engine}/streamdown.json` exists and the registry's `markdown` item is the repair lib consumed through the same renderMarkdown seam. Content follows the docs-site content standards (active voice, terminology lock, austere reference register).
2. GREEN phase — with the page landed, identical commands: assert build exit 0 at exactly RED page count + 1, HTTP 200 at `/components/streamdown` with the main h1 carrying Streamdown and the pinned honest sentence, index page_count exactly RED + 1, and exactly 0 occurrences of `streamdown.json` and of `@react-native-reusables/cli` in the served route HTML; emit `green.json` and `run.json` binding candidate and harness hashes, exact commands, exit codes, and observed counts; stop only owned children on every exit path.
3. Evidence is exactly `.tmp/FIX-ORI-AST-004-1/red.json`, `green.json`, `run.json`.
4. No change to any other file: the search dialog (`apps/docs/src/islands/` + its script), `scripts/docs-data/search-index.ts`, `apps/docs/src/lib/search-page-model.ts`, `apps/docs/src/pages/components/[item].astro`, every existing page, and `human-flows.json` stay byte-unchanged. # Sprint 05: orient-search

**Status:** in_progress  
**Sequence:** 5  
**Timeline:** Phase 2

## Overview

Give a first-time integrator a complete orientation path: Introduction, one engine decision, registry-specific installation and CLI guidance, Theming and Dark mode, one seed-data Quickstart, and a handoff to a real AI SDK v7 example. Connect that content to persistent engine tabs, live theme values, built-site search, registry destinations, and useful missing-page recovery.

Absorb the smallest real prerequisites that make those paths executable: the published PromptInput import graph, both clean Expo consumers, a substantive ownership explanation, actual 404 recovery, the real example API and native composition, canonical registry hosting, and source-bound build and publication checks. This does not add another tutorial or a demonstrated use case. Sprint 06 may deepen the ownership tables; Sprint 11 may deepen resilience and accessibility; later delivery work may harden deployment and rollback.

The plan contains **36 tasks / 131 points**, compared with the roadmap sketch of approximately 12 items / 34–55 points: **76 points above its upper bound**. It retains 13 locked flows, 13 numbered gate steps, and four post-integration journey proofs. Estimates describe the approved prerequisite absorption rather than forcing the work into the sketch.

All implementation, functional RED, product verification, hosted acceptance, and deployment proof are future work. This document records a plan, not a passing gate or release.

## Human Testing Gate

**Gate:** A stranger opening /docs/introduction over the built site's local preview can read in one pass that the library provides universal AI chat and agent UI components for React Native, that it is distributed as a copy-paste registry, and that it is not an npm package.

**Entrypoint:** docs site local preview — built dist served by astro preview (http://localhost:4321) or the pnpm e2e:docs webServer; route /docs/introduction

**Before:** The source snapshot at the planned source SHA already contains Theming and shared layout, header, table, and tab controls. Introduction, Installation, CLI, Dark mode, Quickstart, the ownership-boundary route, and a custom 404 route are absent in that inspected snapshot. Existing Theming content still needs engine-correct claims and the real paired TokenTable. These are planning observations from the source, not current browser results. Each owner must observe the actual functional failure before implementation; the stale roadmap claim that all of these controls are absent is not a RED oracle.

**Success state:** A visitor reads useful, source-backed bodies instead of empty shells, chooses the correct engine once, follows literal registry commands, reads the same information without JavaScript, sees live theme changes without a flash, and reaches real content through keyboard search or missing-page recovery. The single Quickstart reaches a visible seed-data screen and then a separately verified real-provider example. Acceptance also requires the discriminating build checks and fresh native, provider, public-registry, and hosted evidence specified below.

**Demonstrates:** UC-DOCS-01, UC-DOCS-02, UC-SHELL-02, UC-SHELL-01 (TokenTable half), UC-SHELL-03 (prose-persistence half)

**Fixed carryover:** UC-GEND-07 AC-2; TR-12 (full); CAP-DOCS-01 snippet/link build integration. Boundary, recovery, API, and publication work support this projection; they do not expand the demonstrated-use-case list.

# FIX-ORI-AST-004-1: Publish the docs-owned streamdown dependency-explainer destination

## What this does

Lands the one destination the locked search contract names but no task ever owned: a docs-owned, hand-authored dependency explainer at `apps/docs/src/pages/components/streamdown.astro`, served at `/components/streamdown`. ORI-AST-004's pinned search-dialog contract (AC-1..4) and the locked gate flows (`human-flows.json:730,742` — "five existing item destinations" including `/components/streamdown`) treat that route as a real destination: Enter navigation must land at HTTP 200 with a rendered title, and the real Pagefind index must surface it for the query `streamdown`. The registry's 56 items never included streamdown — it is the third-party markdown-rendering dependency the conversation family consumes through the renderMarkdown seam, not a shippable registry item — so the generated `[item].astro` fan-out can never emit the route. This task authors the page directly (a static route wins over the `[item]` dynamic route without touching it), verified through a task-owned proof harness (`tests/sprint-05-orient-search/streamdown-destination-proof.test.ts`) that drives the real build, the pinned real Pagefind run, and the real built preview.

The page is honestly framed: it explains what Streamdown is (the npm package `react-native-streamdown`), why the conversation family depends on it (`MessageResponse` in Message and `ReasoningContent` in Reasoning take a `renderMarkdown` prop; omit it and each renders plain Text, and markdown repair runs before either), how a consumer installs it (the four peers and permissions rendered from the committed `apps/docs/src/data/dev-client-matrix.json` streamdown entry, plus the dev-client verdict), and its registry relationship through the pinned sentence `Streamdown is not a registry item.` — no registry CLI command, no `rnraielements.com/r/{engine}/streamdown.json` target, no InstallCommand, no version chip, no family pager.

## Why

ORI-AST-004 (in flight, blocked cycle 1, checkpoint `b2560ce3`) proved the entire search dialog against the real index — 7 passed / 8 failed, and all 8 failures are the single pinned `/components/streamdown` destination leg: the route is a verified 404 and searching streamdown returns only the two docs pages that mention it. The wave-4 ruling made the resolution human-owned; the human decided (recorded in-session 2026-09-25) to create the docs-owned destination page rather than amend three tasks' ACs plus locked gate steps. Every path to ORI-AST-004's GREEN runs through this page existing at that route in the built dist and the real index. ORI-AST-008 (completed — commit `f5586742`) owns the reference-destination surface whose conventions this page follows; ORI-CONT-005 (completed) authored the boundary prose the page restates and links to. The search dialog, the indexer script, and the page model are write-prohibited to this task — they land with ORI-AST-004's branch, whose eight failing legs flip green once this page reaches trunk.

## How to verify

```sh
pnpm exec tsx tests/sprint-05-orient-search/streamdown-destination-proof.test.ts
pnpm typecheck
pnpm exec biome ci apps/docs/src/pages/components/streamdown.astro tests/sprint-05-orient-search/streamdown-destination-proof.test.ts
```

The first command is the exact selector: the task-owned proof harness — (a) RED phase: on the pre-change candidate it runs the real `pnpm --filter @rnr-ai-elements/docs build`, the pinned real Pagefind run (`pnpm dlx pagefind@1.5.2 --site apps/docs/dist`, the identical invocation ORI-AST-004's indexer uses), and the real built preview over the dist, recording the route's 404, the build page count, and the index page_count; (b) GREEN phase: identical commands with the page landed — build exit 0 at RED page count + 1, HTTP 200 at `/components/streamdown` with the rendered h1 carrying Streamdown and the pinned honest sentence, index page_count exactly RED + 1 (63 → 64 as it lands), and zero registry-command occurrences in the served HTML. The harness stays small — it orchestrates the real commands and does not become a second search gate. `pnpm typecheck` and the scoped Biome command are preserved static gates.

## Scope

Own exactly the new destination page, the task-owned proof harness, plus bounded evidence. The search dialog, `scripts/docs-data/search-index.ts`, `apps/docs/src/lib/search-page-model.ts`, the `[item].astro` template, every existing page, and `human-flows.json` stay byte-unchanged — the locked gate flows now point at a route that will exist; their bytes stay locked.

# Sprint 05: orient-search

**Status:** in_progress  
**Sequence:** 5  
**Timeline:** Phase 2

## Overview

Give a first-time integrator a complete orientation path: Introduction, one engine decision, registry-specific installation and CLI guidance, Theming and Dark mode, one seed-data Quickstart, and a handoff to a real AI SDK v7 example. Connect that content to persistent engine tabs, live theme values, built-site search, registry destinations, and useful missing-page recovery.

Absorb the smallest real prerequisites that make those paths executable: the published PromptInput import graph, both clean Expo consumers, a substantive ownership explanation, actual 404 recovery, the real example API and native composition, canonical registry hosting, and source-bound build and publication checks. This does not add another tutorial or a demonstrated use case. Sprint 06 may deepen the ownership tables; Sprint 11 may deepen resilience and accessibility; later delivery work may harden deployment and rollback.

The plan contains **36 tasks / 131 points**, compared with the roadmap sketch of approximately 12 items / 34–55 points: **76 points above its upper bound**. It retains 13 locked flows, 13 numbered gate steps, and four post-integration journey proofs. Estimates describe the approved prerequisite absorption rather than forcing the work into the sketch.

All implementation, functional RED, product verification, hosted acceptance, and deployment proof are future work. This document records a plan, not a passing gate or release.

## Human Testing Gate

**Gate:** A stranger opening /docs/introduction over the built site's local preview can read in one pass that the library provides universal AI chat and agent UI components for React Native, that it is distributed as a copy-paste registry, and that it is not an npm package.

**Entrypoint:** docs site local preview — built dist served by astro preview (http://localhost:4321) or the pnpm e2e:docs webServer; route /docs/introduction

**Before:** The source snapshot at the planned source SHA already contains Theming and shared layout, header, table, and tab controls. Introduction, Installation, CLI, Dark mode, Quickstart, the ownership-boundary route, and a custom 404 route are absent in that inspected snapshot. Existing Theming content still needs engine-correct claims and the real paired TokenTable. These are planning observations from the source, not current browser results. Each owner must observe the actual functional failure before implementation; the stale roadmap claim that all of these controls are absent is not a RED oracle.

**Success state:** A visitor reads useful, source-backed bodies instead of empty shells, chooses the correct engine once, follows literal registry commands, reads the same information without JavaScript, sees live theme changes without a flash, and reaches real content through keyboard search or missing-page recovery. The single Quickstart reaches a visible seed-data screen and then a separately verified real-provider example. Acceptance also requires the discriminating build checks and fresh native, provider, public-registry, and hosted evidence specified below.

**Demonstrates:** UC-DOCS-01, UC-DOCS-02, UC-SHELL-02, UC-SHELL-01 (TokenTable half), UC-SHELL-03 (prose-persistence half)

**Fixed carryover:** UC-GEND-07 AC-2; TR-12 (full); CAP-DOCS-01 snippet/link build integration. Boundary, recovery, API, and publication work support this projection; they do not expand the demonstrated-use-case list.

# FIX-ORI-AI-001-1: Keep the worked example hook's regenerate payload itemIds unique

## What this does

Fixes the worked example's retry defect at its root. After owned-endpoint loss, the `useLiveChat` hook's clearError-then-regenerate path assembles an outgoing payload containing duplicated assistant message entries that carry repeated OpenAI itemIds in `providerMetadata`; the real OpenAI Responses endpoint rejects that payload and the server emits an error record with 0 deltas. The fix keeps every assistant provider-metadata itemId unique across the outgoing history before the transport serializes the request body.

## Why

ORI-RN-004's cycle-1 blocked report (checkpoint a86231aa) root-caused the iOS/Android retry-completion failure headlessly with the hook's exact SDK classes (`Chat` from @ai-sdk/react 4.0.92 + `DefaultChatTransport` from ai 7.0.89, throttle 50) and bisected it on the real backend: any payload variant leaving each itemId unique completes. Web passes only because its fresh-session path never regenerates with stale history. No pending task owns the hook file — ORI-RN-004's write-allowlist cannot reach `apps/example/lib/use-live-chat.ts`, and ORI-AI-001 is completed — while the gate's locked steps already promise retry completion. The missing piece is this hook-side fix.

## How to verify

Run `pnpm exec tsx tests/sprint-05-orient-search/support/live-chat-regenerate-payload.test.ts` against the real owned backend and the official OpenAI Responses endpoint. The driver imports the real `Chat` + `DefaultChatTransport` classes from apps/example's installed packages, reproduces the endpoint-loss retry state through the owned backend lifecycle, captures the outgoing bodies and the server's sanitized records, and proves functional RED before the fix and GREEN after. Also run the preserved scoped compiler command below.

## Scope

Own the regenerate-payload fix in `apps/example/lib/use-live-chat.ts`, one new scoped driver under `tests/sprint-05-orient-search/support/`, and bounded evidence under `.tmp/FIX-ORI-AI-001-1/`. Rendered retry acceptance on devices remains with ORI-RN-004; the server, the screen and the native drivers stay untouched.

### OUTCOME

After owned-endpoint loss, the worked example hook's Retry (clearError then regenerate) produces an outgoing payload whose assistant providerMetadata itemIds are all unique; the real OpenAI Responses endpoint accepts it and the server records a new completed, provider-correlated answer with exactly 1 retained user turn. The normal send/follow-up path is unchanged.

### CRITICAL CONSTRAINTS — Never

- Never expose OPENAI_API_KEY to client imports, EXPO_PUBLIC variables, install/compiler processes, command arguments or captured evidence. Credentials reach only the trusted launcher and the server child.
- Never mock the thing under test: no mocked Chat, transport, fetch, server or provider. Drive the REAL classes installed for apps/example (ai@7.0.89, @ai-sdk/react@4.0.92) against the REAL backend route and the REAL OpenAI Responses endpoint.
- Never satisfy retry by duplicating the user turn (re-sending via sendMessage), swallowing the error, retrying silently in a loop, or classifying an errored HTTP 200 stream as completed.
- Never weaken the consumer oracle: the fixed retry must deliver a new real request ID, a completed provider-correlated answer, and exactly 1 retained user turn.
- Never strip or rewrite legitimate unique itemIds or remove message text/parts such that contextual history breaks (the follow-up must still retain the nonce).
- Never write outside the exact allowlist: NOT apps/example/server/**, NOT ORI-RN-004's screen/driver files, NOT ORI-AI-001's or ORI-RN-004's evidence directories, NOT the planning-owned surface policy.
- Never upgrade dependencies by default. Only a pinned real version with evidence from the installed packages that no hook-level fix can work; never "latest", never a forced alias.

### DONE WHEN

- [ ] AC-1 proves functional RED (duplicated-itemId payload → real provider rejection, 0 deltas) and GREEN (unique itemIds → new real request ID, completed provider-correlated record, exactly 1 retained user turn) on the real stack.
- [ ] AC-2 proves the happy path, hook contract, scoped compiler and exact scope compliance are preserved.
- [ ] The exact selector and preserved commands pass; independent review confirms canonical functional RED, seeded evidence and no stubs.

### SPECIFICATION

Remediate the ORI-AI-001 hook so the regenerate path emits provider-acceptable history. The defect: after a failed turn (endpoint loss), the outgoing regenerate payload contains duplicated assistant entries carrying repeated OpenAI itemIds in providerMetadata; the OpenAI Responses endpoint rejects it. The fix is a hook-level sanitize/stabilize of the outgoing history at the transport seam in `apps/example/lib/use-live-chat.ts`. Dependency installation ownership and the server stay with ORI-AI-001's landed surface; this task changes only the hook and adds one scoped driver.

### BOUNDARY CONTRACTS

1. Fix the root cause in `apps/example/lib/use-live-chat.ts`: keep every assistant provider-metadata itemId unique across the outgoing (regenerate) history before the transport serializes the body. The installed `HttpChatTransport` accepts `prepareSendMessagesRequest({ id, messages, trigger, messageId })` and returns the prepared request body (apps/example/node_modules/ai/src/ui/http-chat-transport.ts, lines 106-158) — pass it to the existing `new DefaultChatTransport({ api, fetch, ... })` construction; an equivalent transport-level sanitize inside the hook module is acceptable. Editing the server is not.
2. Sanitize semantics: keep the first occurrence of each itemId and strip the stale duplicates, or an equivalent uniqueness-preserving transform. Never invent provider itemIds, never remove message text, parts, or legitimate unique metadata.
3. Preserve the public hook contract from ORI-AI-001 AC-4: `messages`, `status`, `error`, `sendMessage`, `stop`, `regenerate`, `clearError`; retry makes 2 ordered calls `clearError()` then `regenerate()`; throttle 50; 0 initial messages; stable `DefaultChatTransport` with `expo/fetch`; absolute `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` validation appending `/api/chat`.
4. The scoped driver must exercise the REAL `Chat` + `DefaultChatTransport` classes resolved from the apps/example workspace packages (pnpm layout; ORI-RN-004 cycle-1 recorded that `ai` resolves only from apps/example's node_modules and its probes imported by absolute worktree path). The sanitize logic itself must live in and be exported from `apps/example/lib/use-live-chat.ts`. If the top-level `expo/fetch` import blocks headless import of the hook module outside Expo, a lazy dynamic import inside `chatFetch` is the allowed enabler — runtime behavior in Expo must stay identical.
5. Reuse `tests/sprint-05-orient-search/support/live-backend.ts` for backend launch/stop/restart; act only on recorded owned PIDs. The server emits sanitized records only at stream termination (apps/example/server/chat.ts finally block), so assertions await record emission rather than polling mid-stream.
6. Keep evidence under `.tmp/FIX-ORI-AI-001-1/` only, bounded and sanitized (request IDs, outcome, response IDs, delta counts, itemId-uniqueness results; never credentials or raw provider errors).

### ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA — RED → GREEN → REFACTOR

Only AC-1 is PRIMARY. Both criteria run on the same real stack in one scoped driver.

# FIX-ORI-AI-001-1: Keep the worked example hook's regenerate payload itemIds unique

## What this does

Fixes the worked example's retry defect at its root. After owned-endpoint loss, the `useLiveChat` hook's clearError-then-regenerate path assembles an outgoing payload containing duplicated assistant message entries that carry repeated OpenAI itemIds in `providerMetadata`; the real OpenAI Responses endpoint rejects that payload and the server emits an error record with 0 deltas. The fix keeps every assistant provider-metadata itemId unique across the outgoing history before the transport serializes the request body.

## Why

ORI-RN-004's cycle-1 blocked report (checkpoint a86231aa) root-caused the iOS/Android retry-completion failure headlessly with the hook's exact SDK classes (`Chat` from @ai-sdk/react 4.0.92 + `DefaultChatTransport` from ai 7.0.89, throttle 50) and bisected it on the real backend: any payload variant leaving each itemId unique completes. Web passes only because its fresh-session path never regenerates with stale history. No pending task owns the hook file — ORI-RN-004's write-allowlist cannot reach `apps/example/lib/use-live-chat.ts`, and ORI-AI-001 is completed — while the gate's locked steps already promise retry completion. The missing piece is this hook-side fix.

## How to verify

Run `pnpm exec tsx tests/sprint-05-orient-search/support/live-chat-regenerate-payload.test.ts` against the real owned backend and the official OpenAI Responses endpoint. The driver imports the real `Chat` + `DefaultChatTransport` classes from apps/example's installed packages, reproduces the endpoint-loss retry state through the owned backend lifecycle, captures the outgoing bodies and the server's sanitized records, and proves functional RED before the fix and GREEN after. Also run the preserved scoped compiler command below.

## Scope

Own the regenerate-payload fix in `apps/example/lib/use-live-chat.ts`, one new scoped driver under `tests/sprint-05-orient-search/support/`, and bounded evidence under `.tmp/FIX-ORI-AI-001-1/`. Rendered retry acceptance on devices remains with ORI-RN-004; the server, the screen and the native drivers stay untouched.

# Sprint 05: orient-search

**Status:** in_progress  
**Sequence:** 5  
**Timeline:** Phase 2

## Overview

Give a first-time integrator a complete orientation path: Introduction, one engine decision, registry-specific installation and CLI guidance, Theming and Dark mode, one seed-data Quickstart, and a handoff to a real AI SDK v7 example. Connect that content to persistent engine tabs, live theme values, built-site search, registry destinations, and useful missing-page recovery.

Absorb the smallest real prerequisites that make those paths executable: the published PromptInput import graph, both clean Expo consumers, a substantive ownership explanation, actual 404 recovery, the real example API and native composition, canonical registry hosting, and source-bound build and publication checks. This does not add another tutorial or a demonstrated use case. Sprint 06 may deepen the ownership tables; Sprint 11 may deepen resilience and accessibility; later delivery work may harden deployment and rollback.

The plan contains **36 tasks / 131 points**, compared with the roadmap sketch of approximately 12 items / 34–55 points: **76 points above its upper bound**. It retains 13 locked flows, 13 numbered gate steps, and four post-integration journey proofs. Estimates describe the approved prerequisite absorption rather than forcing the work into the sketch.

All implementation, functional RED, product verification, hosted acceptance, and deployment proof are future work. This document records a plan, not a passing gate or release.

**Gate:** A stranger opening /docs/introduction over the built site's local preview can read in one pass that the library provides universal AI chat and agent UI components for React Native, that it is distributed as a copy-paste registry, and that it is not an npm package.

**Entrypoint:** docs site local preview — built dist served by astro preview (http://localhost:4321) or the pnpm e2e:docs webServer; route /docs/introduction

**Before:** The source snapshot at the planned source SHA already contains Theming and shared layout, header, table, and tab controls. Introduction, Installation, CLI, Dark mode, Quickstart, the ownership-boundary route, and a custom 404 route are absent in that inspected snapshot. Existing Theming content still needs engine-correct claims and the real paired TokenTable. These are planning observations from the source, not current browser results. Each owner must observe the actual functional failure before implementation; the stale roadmap claim that all of these controls are absent is not a RED oracle.

**Success state:** A visitor reads useful, source-backed bodies instead of empty shells, chooses the correct engine once, follows literal registry commands, reads the same information without JavaScript, sees live theme changes without a flash, and reaches real content through keyboard search or missing-page recovery. The single Quickstart reaches a visible seed-data screen and then a separately verified real-provider example. Acceptance also requires the discriminating build checks and fresh native, provider, public-registry, and hosted evidence specified below.

**Demonstrates:** UC-DOCS-01, UC-DOCS-02, UC-SHELL-02, UC-SHELL-01 (TokenTable half), UC-SHELL-03 (prose-persistence half)

# FIX-ORI-RN-005-1: Make the canonical live-chat sources compile in the independent NativeWind consumer

## What this does

Fixes the two compile defects that block ORI-RN-005's clean-consumer proof. In the prescribed independent NativeWind consumer — fresh Expo 57 root outside the monorepo from ORI-RN-001's committed template, registry items from the literal public recipe, the verified hook pins, and the five canonical app sources copied byte-identical — the consumer's own `tsc --noEmit` rejects with exactly two errors, both in landed files outside ORI-RN-005's write scope:

1. `apps/example/components/live-chat-screen.tsx:5` — `import { useUniwind } from 'uniwind'` → TS2307 in a consumer that never adds uniwind. The hook's only use is `theme === 'dark' ? 'dark' : 'light'` feeding `THEME[mode].background`; the behavior-preserving fix is React Native's `useColorScheme`.
2. `packages/docs-snippets/nativewind/lib/theme.ts:8` — `const THEME` is not exported while the canonical screen imports `{ THEME } from '@/lib/theme'` (apps/example's own lib/theme.ts exports it) → TS2459. One-word fix: `export const THEME`.

## Why

ORI-RN-005's cycle-1 blocked report (checkpoint 20f4b6a6) proved everything else green and root-caused the failure to exactly these two errors. No pending task can fix them: ORI-RN-005's write allowlist excludes `apps/example/**` and `packages/docs-snippets/nativewind/**` except its package.json; ORI-RN-001, ORI-RN-004 and ORI-AI-001 are completed. Behavior preservation is grounded in the landed code: apps/example's only theme control (`apps/example/gallery/chrome.tsx`) flips the app via `Appearance.setColorScheme` — exactly the signal `useColorScheme()` tracks — and the NativeWind consumer root (`packages/docs-snippets/nativewind/app/_layout.tsx`) already themes via `useColorScheme()`. After this lands, ORI-RN-005 reruns its blocked legs with no further work in its own files.

## How to verify

Run `pnpm exec tsx .tmp/FIX-ORI-RN-005-1/consumer-compile-proof.ts` — the task-owned scratch harness that materializes the prescribed consumer, copies the five canonical sources byte-identical (SHA-256 pairs), runs the consumer's `tsc --noEmit` (functional RED pre-fix with exactly the two named errors, GREEN post-fix), and records the preserved repository checks. Also run the preserved commands below.

## Scope

Own the two one-line fixes in `apps/example/components/live-chat-screen.tsx` and `packages/docs-snippets/nativewind/lib/theme.ts`, plus the scratch harness and bounded evidence under `.tmp/FIX-ORI-RN-005-1/`. On-device behavior remains ORI-RN-005's rerun and ORI-AI-002's matrix; every ORI-RN-005 in-flight file stays untouched.

# Sprint 05: orient-search

**Status:** in_progress  
**Sequence:** 5  
**Timeline:** Phase 2

## Overview

Give a first-time integrator a complete orientation path: Introduction, one engine decision, registry-specific installation and CLI guidance, Theming and Dark mode, one seed-data Quickstart, and a handoff to a real AI SDK v7 example. Connect that content to persistent engine tabs, live theme values, built-site search, registry destinations, and useful missing-page recovery.

Absorb the smallest real prerequisites that make those paths executable: the published PromptInput import graph, both clean Expo consumers, a substantive ownership explanation, actual 404 recovery, the real example API and native composition, canonical registry hosting, and source-bound build and publication checks. This does not add another tutorial or a demonstrated use case. Sprint 06 may deepen the ownership tables; Sprint 11 may deepen resilience and accessibility; later delivery work may harden deployment and rollback.

The plan contains **36 tasks / 131 points**, compared with the roadmap sketch of approximately 12 items / 34–55 points: **76 points above its upper bound**. It retains 13 locked flows, 13 numbered gate steps, and four post-integration journey proofs. Estimates describe the approved prerequisite absorption rather than forcing the work into the sketch.

All implementation, functional RED, product verification, hosted acceptance, and deployment proof are future work. This document records a plan, not a passing gate or release.

## Human Testing Gate

**Gate:** A stranger opening /docs/introduction over the built site's local preview can read in one pass that the library provides universal AI chat and agent UI components for React Native, that it is distributed as a copy-paste registry, and that it is not an npm package.

**Entrypoint:** docs site local preview — built dist served by astro preview (http://localhost:4321) or the pnpm e2e:docs webServer; route /docs/introduction

**Before:** The source snapshot at the planned source SHA already contains Theming and shared layout, header, table, and tab controls. Introduction, Installation, CLI, Dark mode, Quickstart, the ownership-boundary route, and a custom 404 route are absent in that inspected snapshot. Existing Theming content still needs engine-correct claims and the real paired TokenTable. These are planning observations from the source, not current browser results. Each owner must observe the actual functional failure before implementation; the stale roadmap claim that all of these controls are absent is not a RED oracle.

**Success state:** A visitor reads useful, source-backed bodies instead of empty shells, chooses the correct engine once, follows literal registry commands, reads the same information without JavaScript, sees live theme changes without a flash, and reaches real content through keyboard search or missing-page recovery. The single Quickstart reaches a visible seed-data screen and then a separately verified real-provider example. Acceptance also requires the discriminating build checks and fresh native, provider, public-registry, and hosted evidence specified below.

**Demonstrates:** UC-DOCS-01, UC-DOCS-02, UC-SHELL-02, UC-SHELL-01 (TokenTable half), UC-SHELL-03 (prose-persistence half)

**Fixed carryover:** UC-GEND-07 AC-2; TR-12 (full); CAP-DOCS-01 snippet/link build integration. Boundary, recovery, API, and publication work support this projection; they do not expand the demonstrated-use-case list.

# FIX-ORI-RN-005-1: Make the canonical live-chat sources compile in the independent NativeWind consumer

## What this does

Fixes the two compile defects that block ORI-RN-005's clean-consumer proof. In the prescribed independent NativeWind consumer — fresh Expo 57 root outside the monorepo from ORI-RN-001's committed template, registry items from the literal public recipe, the verified hook pins, and the five canonical app sources copied byte-identical — the consumer's own `tsc --noEmit` rejects with exactly two errors, both in landed files outside ORI-RN-005's write scope:

1. `apps/example/components/live-chat-screen.tsx:5` — `import { useUniwind } from 'uniwind'` → TS2307 in a consumer that never adds uniwind. The hook's only use is `theme === 'dark' ? 'dark' : 'light'` feeding `THEME[mode].background`; the behavior-preserving fix is React Native's `useColorScheme`.
2. `packages/docs-snippets/nativewind/lib/theme.ts:8` — `const THEME` is not exported while the canonical screen imports `{ THEME } from '@/lib/theme'` (apps/example's own lib/theme.ts exports it) → TS2459. One-word fix: `export const THEME`.

## Why

ORI-RN-005's cycle-1 blocked report (checkpoint 20f4b6a6) proved everything else green and root-caused the failure to exactly these two errors. No pending task can fix them: ORI-RN-005's write allowlist excludes `apps/example/**` and `packages/docs-snippets/nativewind/**` except its package.json; ORI-RN-001, ORI-RN-004 and ORI-AI-001 are completed. Behavior preservation is grounded in the landed code: apps/example's only theme control (`apps/example/gallery/chrome.tsx`) flips the app via `Appearance.setColorScheme` — exactly the signal `useColorScheme()` tracks — and the NativeWind consumer root (`packages/docs-snippets/nativewind/app/_layout.tsx`) already themes via `useColorScheme()`. After this lands, ORI-RN-005 reruns its blocked legs with no further work in its own files.

## How to verify

Run `pnpm exec tsx .tmp/FIX-ORI-RN-005-1/consumer-compile-proof.ts` — the task-owned scratch harness that materializes the prescribed consumer, copies the five canonical sources byte-identical (SHA-256 pairs), runs the consumer's `tsc --noEmit` (functional RED pre-fix with exactly the two named errors, GREEN post-fix), and records the preserved repository checks. Also run the preserved commands below.

## Scope

Own the two one-line fixes in `apps/example/components/live-chat-screen.tsx` and `packages/docs-snippets/nativewind/lib/theme.ts`, plus the scratch harness and bounded evidence under `.tmp/FIX-ORI-RN-005-1/`. On-device behavior remains ORI-RN-005's rerun and ORI-AI-002's matrix; every ORI-RN-005 in-flight file stays untouched.
